title: Composing with Intention: Notes on Learning Jetpack Compose
excerpt: A few recurring patterns I keep reaching for after weeks of reading Compose source and rebuilding the same three screens.
bodyMarkdown:
Every time I sit down to read someone else's Compose code, I end up with three or four snippets I want to remember and one idea for a post I never quite get around to writing. This is the first attempt at actually writing one of them down properly.

The pattern that keeps showing up is state hoisting done *just* far enough - not all the way to the top of the tree, but exactly to the nearest ancestor that needs to coordinate two siblings. Getting that distance right is most of what makes a Compose screen feel simple to reason about later.

> Hoist state only as far as the nearest shared ancestor that actually needs it - no further.

A second pattern: `remember` plus a stable key is doing more work than it looks like. Most of the recomposition bugs I've hit trace back to a key that wasn't as stable as I assumed - a lambda captured fresh every recomposition, or a data class missing an override I needed.

None of this is exotic. It's the kind of thing you only really internalize by re-deriving it from a bug, which is exactly why capturing the idea in the moment - before the article tab closes - matters more than it seems like it should.
